prompt:
A desktop website home page, rendered edge to edge at 16:9 with crisp readable text, no browser window, device or desk around it. It is the portfolio of Giannia, an architecture student. Visitors (architecture firms and grad-school admissions) come to see her work quickly and open a project.

The page IS a sketchbook made of yellow tracing paper lying on a glowing white light table. Pale canary trace sheets, slightly translucent, overlap so lower sheets show through as faint layers; soft cool-white light glows from beneath. Ink is graphite pencil grey; notes in non-photo-blue pencil; one red pencil mark for the active state.

What leads: a catalog of her works as die-cut vinyl stickers pressed onto the top trace sheet, each sticker a small crisp architectural image (a plan drawing, a white chipboard model photo, a section, a watercolour sketch, a page of an essay) with a thin white kiss-cut border. One featured sticker, "Bathhouse on the Canal", is twice the size of the others. Each sticker has a short handwritten pencil note connected to it by a thin leader line, like an annotation on a drawing: "Studio III, 2025", "chipboard, 1:50", "essay, 4,000 words". A few stickers sit faded beneath a second trace sheet, as if filtered out.

Frame: top left, "Giannia" in neat architectural hand lettering with "works & words, 2022–2026" under it; along the left edge, filter tabs written in pencil like index tabs: All, Studio projects, Models, Sketches, Writing, Competitions; top right small links "Index", "About", "Contact"; a tiny title-block in the bottom right corner reading "Sheet 01 of 01 · placeholder works".
